assertTrue(Modifier.isPublic(CharSet.class.getModifiers())); assertFalse(Modifier.isFinal(CharSet.class.getModifiers()));
// "abc" -> three single-character ranges Set<CharRange> ranges = rangesOf("abc"); assertEquals(3, ranges.size());
// "a-ce-f" -> two adjacent multi-character ranges ranges = rangesOf("a-ce-f"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "ae-f" -> a single character followed by a range ranges = rangesOf("ae-f"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "e-fa" -> a range followed by a single character ranges = rangesOf("e-fa"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "ae-fm-pz" -> singles and ranges interleaved ranges = rangesOf("ae-fm-pz"); assertEquals(4, ranges.size());
// "^abc" -> negated single 'a', then plain 'b' and 'c' Set<CharRange> ranges = rangesOf("^abc"); assertEquals(3, ranges.size());
// "b^ac" -> negation may appear mid-string ranges = rangesOf("b^ac"); assertEquals(3, ranges.size());
// "db^ac" -> leading single before a mid-string negation ranges = rangesOf("db^ac"); assertEquals(4, ranges.size());
// "^b^a" -> two negated singles ranges = rangesOf("^b^a"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "b^a-c^z" -> single, negated range, then negated single ranges = rangesOf("b^a-c^z"); assertEquals(3, ranges.size());
// "a-^c" parses as range "a-^" plus single "c" CharSet set = CharSet.getInstance("a-^c"); Set<CharRange> ranges = set.getCharRanges();
// "^a-^c" parses as negated range "^a-^" plus single "c" set = CharSet.getInstance("^a-^c"); ranges = set.getCharRanges();
// "a- ^-- " parses as range "a- " plus negated range "^-- "; together covers everything set = CharSet.getInstance("a- ^-- "); ranges = set.getCharRanges();
// "^-b" parses as the plain range "^-b" (the leading ^ is the range start, not a negation) set = CharSet.getInstance("^-b"); ranges = set.getCharRanges();
// "b-^" parses as range "b-^", reversed internally to "^-b" set = CharSet.getInstance("b-^"); ranges = set.getCharRanges();
// A lone or repeated dash collapses to the single character '-' Set<CharRange> ranges = rangesOf("-"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
ranges = rangesOf("--"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.is('-')));
ranges = rangesOf("---"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.is('-')));
ranges = rangesOf("----"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.is('-')));
// "-a" -> two separate single characters ranges = rangesOf("-a"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "a-" -> two separate single characters ranges = rangesOf("a-"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "a--" -> range from 'a' to '-' ranges = rangesOf("a--"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "--a" -> range from '-' to 'a' ranges = rangesOf("--a"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "^" alone is the literal single character '^' Set<CharRange> ranges = rangesOf("^"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "^^" -> negated '^' ranges = rangesOf("^^"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "^^^" -> negated '^' followed by literal '^' ranges = rangesOf("^^^"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "^^^^" -> two identical negated '^' that collapse into one ranges = rangesOf("^^^^"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "a^" -> literal 'a' and literal '^' ranges = rangesOf("a^"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "^a-" -> negated 'a' followed by literal '-' ranges = rangesOf("^a-"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "^^-c" -> negated range from '^' to 'c' ranges = rangesOf("^^-c"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "^c-^" -> negated range from 'c' to '^' ranges = rangesOf("^c-^"); assertEquals(1, ranges.size());
// "^c-^d" -> negated range "^c-^" plus literal 'd' ranges = rangesOf("^c-^d"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// "^^-" -> negated '^' followed by literal '-' ranges = rangesOf("^^-"); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
// null and "" both yield the empty set CharSet set = CharSet.getInstance((String) null); assertEquals("[]", set.toString());
set = CharSet.getInstance(""); assertEquals("[]", set.toString()); assertEquals(0, set.getCharRanges().size());
// single literal character set = CharSet.getInstance("a"); assertEquals("[a]", set.toString());
// negated single character set = CharSet.getInstance("^a"); assertEquals("[^a]", set.toString());
// plain range set = CharSet.getInstance("a-e"); assertEquals("[a-e]", set.toString());
// negated range set = CharSet.getInstance("^a-e"); assertEquals("[^a-e]", set.toString());
final CharSet btod = CharSet.getInstance("b-d"); final CharSet dtob = CharSet.getInstance("d-b"); final CharSet bcd = CharSet.getInstance("bcd");
// range "b-d" contains b, c, d but not the surrounding characters assertFalse(btod.contains('a')); assertTrue(btod.contains('b'));
// explicit set "bcd" behaves the same as the range assertFalse(bcd.contains('a')); assertTrue(bcd.contains('b'));
// "bd" only contains b and d, not c in between assertFalse(bd.contains('a')); assertTrue(bd.contains('b'));
// "^b-d" is the complement of "b-d" assertTrue(notbtod.contains('a')); assertFalse(notbtod.contains('b'));
// "d-b" is reversed to "b-d" and therefore behaves identically assertFalse(dtob.contains('a')); assertTrue(dtob.contains('b'));
assertEquals("[b-d]", dtob.toString()); assertEquals(1, dtob.getCharRanges().size());
final CharSet abc = CharSet.getInstance("abc"); final CharSet abc2 = CharSet.getInstance("abc"); final CharSet atoc = CharSet.getInstance("a-c");
assertNotEquals(null, abc);
// "abc" equals itself and an equally-defined set, but not a differently-defined one assertEquals(abc, abc); assertEquals(abc, abc2);
// "a-c" is not equal to the enumerated "abc" even though they match the same characters assertNotEquals(atoc, abc); assertEquals(atoc, atoc);
// "^a-c" is distinct from both of the above assertNotEquals(notatoc, abc); assertNotEquals(notatoc, atoc);
// Known patterns are interned and return the shared constant instance assertSame(CharSet.EMPTY, CharSet.getInstance((String) null)); assertSame(CharSet.EMPTY, CharSet.getInstance((String[]) null));
assertEquals("[]", CharSet.getInstance((String[]) null).toString()); assertEquals("[]", CharSet.getInstance().toString()); assertEquals("[]", CharSet.getInstance(new String[] {null}).toString());
final CharSet abc = CharSet.getInstance("abc"); final CharSet abc2 = CharSet.getInstance("abc"); final CharSet atoc = CharSet.getInstance("a-c");
// equal sets must produce equal hash codes assertEquals(abc.hashCode(), abc.hashCode()); assertEquals(abc.hashCode(), abc2.hashCode());
// Mirrors the negation examples documented on CharSet.getInstance assertFalse(CharSet.getInstance("^a-c").contains('a')); assertTrue(CharSet.getInstance("^a-c").contains('d'));
// A round-tripped clone must equal the original CharSet set = CharSet.getInstance("a"); assertEquals(set, SerializationUtils.clone(set));
// EMPTY has no ranges Set<CharRange> ranges = CharSet.EMPTY.getCharRanges(); assertEquals(0, ranges.size());
// ASCII_ALPHA combines the lower and upper case ranges ranges = CharSet.ASCII_ALPHA.getCharRanges(); assertEquals(2, ranges.size());
ranges = CharSet.ASCII_ALPHA_LOWER.getCharRanges(); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.isIn('a', 'z')));
ranges = CharSet.ASCII_ALPHA_UPPER.getCharRanges(); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.isIn('A', 'Z')));
ranges = CharSet.ASCII_NUMERIC.getCharRanges(); assertEquals(1, ranges.size()); assertTrue(ranges.contains(CharRange.isIn('0', '9')));
